To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
decreased light availability amplifies negative impacts of ocean acidi- fication on calcifying coral organisms.

the negative effects of low-light availability and ocean acidification on corals are additive and that low light availability can amplify the negative impacts of ocean acidi- fication on calcifying coral-reef organisms.
the negative impacts of oceanic and local stressors on calcifying coral-reef organisms are additive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between 2 global stressors (OA and reduced light availability) on 2 calcifying species (coral and alga) that are key components of tropical coral reefs.
the interplay between 2 stressors that coral reef organisms are simultaneously affected by, i.e. ocean acidification and decreased light availability.
the individual and interactive effects of light availability and pCO2 on 2 calcifying reef organisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combined effects of OA and light reduction are not additive or antagonistic but rather synergistic, as they both lead to a decrease of the organisms' calcification.
the negative effects of low irradiance and OA on coral reefs are additive, but that OA has a greater negative impact than light reduction on calcifying organisms.
OA and low light have a negative impact on calcifying organisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
decreased light avail- ability can amplify negative impacts on coral calcification and respiration rates, and that calcifying organisms are affected by OA and low light in different ways.
OA and low light are additive stressors, which can lead to a reduction in the calcification of both calcifying coral reef taxa.
decreased light availability can amplify the negative impacts of OA on calcifying coral-reef organisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of low light availability on coral reefs are not likely to be alleviated by OA, as has sometimes been suggested, but may be amplified.
decreased light availability can amplify the negative impacts of OA on coral reef organisms.
OA and low light can have additive negative effects on calcification and weight gain of calcifying reef organisms.
